inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,419 normalized lines. The paper gives a coherent RH-conditional sharp moment argument: it turns a random-Euler-product heuristic into a multiscale partition of a long prime polynomial, controls typical and first-bad-block regions by direct exponential moments and prime-pairing orthogonality, isolates the fluctuating prime-square term with a second exceptional-set decomposition, transfers the architecture to a quadratic-character family, and diagnoses why the rigorous implicit constant is much worse than the random-matrix prediction. Display extraction is visually fragmented in places, but the prose, stated results, and proof transitions recover the selected mechanisms.

sections_inspected.label: Title and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Front matter states the sharp conditional moment bound and contrasts the many-polynomial direct-moment method with the earlier single-polynomial large-values route.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States Theorem 1, develops the random Euler-product and independent-increment heuristic, identifies two losses in the prior method, and previews the multiscale direct-moment repair and constant problem.

sections_inspected.label: Some tools
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Supplies the RH-conditional Dirichlet-polynomial majorant for log zeta and the cosine-product mean-value rule whose main term is supported on even prime multiplicities.

sections_inspected.label: Outline and deduction of Theorem 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines geometric prime blocks and the good/first-bad partition, states the three integral lemmas, and combines them with the log-zeta majorant to prove the moment bound.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of Lemma 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Controls the good set by positive squared exponential truncations, converts the integral to prime-pairing combinatorics, and reassembles the main term into an Euler-product exponential.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of Lemma 2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses a high even power of the first oversized block as a witness and obtains an exponential penalty that makes every bad stratum summable.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of Lemma 3
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces dyadic exceptional sets for the prime-square polynomial and proves that its extra fluctuation can be absorbed without spoiling the sharp logarithmic exponent.

sections_inspected.label: Other moments of L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Extracts a two-tool portability criterion and instantiates it for quadratic Dirichlet L-functions, explaining the altered square-prime contribution and resulting symmetry exponent.

sections_inspected.label: Implicit constant
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Tracks the double-exponential rigorous constant, compares it with random-matrix factors, optimizes the Gaussian Euler-product heuristic, and locates the unavailable long-polynomial estimate.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgements and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-substantive end matter checked and excluded from semantic units.

accepted_units.title: Square the truncated exponential before enlarging the domain
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how bounded block values permit short exponential series while writing each exponential as a square makes the truncated integrand nonnegative, so integration over the good set can safely be enlarged to the full interval.

accepted_units.title: Prime pairing converts the analytic integral into a multiplicative product
accepted_units.why_material: Expands all block polynomials, verifies the total Dirichlet length is short enough for the mean-value error, uses even-multiplicity pairing and coefficient domination, and reassembles the surviving main terms blockwise.
accepted_units.context_note: This span carries the full bridge from the positive polynomial integral to the square-supported combinatorial sum; the final evaluation is separated into the next unit.

accepted_units.title: Square support collapses multiplicities to the Gaussian exponential
accepted_units.why_material: Restricts to even total degree, computes the correction for repeated primes, and bounds the result by exp(k squared times the prime harmonic sum), yielding the sharp log-power.
accepted_units.context_note: Completes the Lemma 1 mechanism after the preceding orthogonality reduction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: factorial and multiplicity displays are formula-dependent, although the square-support conclusion and final exponential bound are legible.

accepted_units.title: An oversized block becomes its own high-moment penalty
accepted_units.why_material: On each first-bad stratum, inserts a high even power of the offending block, uses disjoint prime ranges and the same pairing calculus, and obtains a penalty exponential in inverse block scale that dominates the truncation cost.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof is a deliberate modification of Lemma 1, so its reusable contribution is the witness-power and penalty mechanism rather than repeated algebra.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: quantitative exponents and products are display-dependent; the prose still identifies independence from the later cutoff and the source of the error term.

accepted_units.title: Dyadic control of the fluctuating prime-square term
accepted_units.why_material: Builds a second good/first-bad hierarchy for dyadic prime-square pieces, discards very large scales by measure and Cauchy-Schwarz, and combines the remaining high-moment penalty with disjointness from the main prime sum.
accepted_units.context_note: This isolates why the secondary polynomial in the log-zeta majorant cannot simply be treated as a uniform constant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: powers and dyadic sums are extraction-fragmented, but definitions, range reductions, and the final summability claim are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Porting the two-tool architecture to quadratic Dirichlet L-functions
accepted_units.why_material: States the family moment bound, replaces time orthogonality by character square-detection, explains why prime squares contribute a fixed shift rather than a fluctuating polynomial, and reconstructs the good/bad block proof with the resulting exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1; the unchecked possible extensions after line 1218 remain supporting context only.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: proposition and family-sum displays are fragmented, but reciprocity, square detection, and the proof adaptation are clearly described.

accepted_units.title: The shortest terminal block drives the double-exponential constant
accepted_units.why_material: Tracks constants through good and bad strata and shows that the main loss comes from the terminal scale forced to be exponentially small in k, producing a double-exponential dependence.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the rigorous diagnostic before comparison with conjectural models.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the bound is display-heavy, while the dominant-term diagnosis and scale relation are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Random-matrix arithmetic and matrix factors predict a much smaller constant
accepted_units.why_material: Records the conjectural moment constant as arithmetic and random-matrix factors and identifies their large-k decay, creating a quantitative benchmark for the proof's loss.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit is a comparison benchmark, not evidence that the conjectured asymptotic has been proved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: Euler and gamma products require the displayed formulas; asymptotic roles are explained in prose.

accepted_units.title: Optimizing the Gaussian Euler-product length recovers the predicted decay
accepted_units.why_material: Treats the prime polynomial as Gaussian, balances the majorant penalty against its variance, selects length T to the power 2 over k, recovers the expected large-k constant scale, and pinpoints the missing long-polynomial control in the bad-block lemma.
accepted_units.context_note: This is explicitly conjectural and neglects zero effects and small-prime non-Gaussian structure; it diagnoses a method limit rather than proving the constant.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From independent prime increments to a deterministic multiscale moment bound
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof operationalizes the random model without assuming it: decreasing block variances license decreasing truncation degrees, positivity permits full-interval integration, and even-prime pairing supplies the Gaussian exponential combinatorially.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The bridge is conditional on the log-zeta majorant under RH and only proves an upper bound; it does not establish a distributional Gaussian limit.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: First-bad-block localization pays for an otherwise illegal long polynomial
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Partitioning by the first oversized block converts failure of typical control into a high-moment witness whose exponential penalty more than pays the majorant's shorter-cutoff cost.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The available penalty forces an exponentially small terminal scale in k and is precisely where sharp dependence of the implicit constant is lost.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A secondary fluctuating term needs its own scale hierarchy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The prime-square part of the zeta majorant is not uniformly bounded, so a dyadic good/first-bad partition is nested around it and coupled to the main prime sum through disjoint supports.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This mechanism is specific to the form of the zeta majorant; in the quadratic-character family the square contribution becomes an essentially fixed logarithmic shift.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Two replacement interfaces determine family portability
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The multiscale proof transfers when a family supplies both a one-sided short-prime majorant for log L and a mean-value rule that detects the relevant diagonal or square configurations.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper works out the quadratic-character case and only conjectures portability to additional families without checking all details.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Constant mismatch isolates the unresolved analytic capacity
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Random-matrix and Gaussian Euler-product pictures agree on a much smaller large-k scale; optimizing the heuristic exposes that rigor would need control of prime polynomials as long as T to the power 2 over k.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The Gaussian calculation neglects zeros and treats small primes too generously, so agreement of scales is a diagnostic rather than a proof of the full conjectural constant.
